questions.question: Who identifies the hazard class of a hazardous material?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the product's identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class, and packing group. The shipper must also determine the correct packaging, labels, markings, and placards.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper must package, mark, and label hazardous materials. The shipper must also supply all necessary placards.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must appear?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging containing the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If the letter "G" (for "Generic") appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, the technical name of the hazardous material must also be listed.

questions.question: Where should placards be placed on a truck?

options.text: On the left and right sides

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: To decide which placard(s) to use when carrying hazardous materials, you must know:

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials
The types of containers being used

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials
questions.explanation: Placards show the hazard classes of materials being carried on a vehicle.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials employees must be trained and tested at least once every three years. Drivers must learn about the risks and how to respond to security threats.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion
How many people should respond to an accident

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include: descriptions and technical names of materials; health hazards; risks of fire or explosion; steps to take in an accident; how to handle fires; how to handle spills or leaks; and first aid measures.

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Many materials become more dangerous if their temperature increases.

questions.question: When you are sitting behind the steering wheel, shipping papers should be:

options.text: Taped to the passenger's side window

questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch in the driver's side door or in another easy-to-reach location while your seat belt is fastened. Papers must be easily visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When accepting a package of hazardous materials, a driver should check that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages
The shipping paper is written in code
All packages are labeled as poison

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping papers to the markings and labels on the packages.

questions.question: Who is responsible for putting placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The shipper provides the placards. The driver is responsible for placing them on the vehicle.

questions.question: A person watching tank loading or unloading must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: The supervisor must stay alert, have a clear view, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank. Wearing a chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: If transporting explosives, you may leave your vehicle unattended only:
questions.explanation: A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives. You may only leave your vehicle there.

questions.question: Which type of material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials require a transport index. This number shows how much control is needed during transport. The total transport index in one vehicle cannot exceed 50.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in the trailer, the trailer should be:
questions.explanation: Parts of a vehicle exposed to corrosive materials must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: When loading or unloading explosive materials, you should:

options.text: Use sharp tools to open packages.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before loading or unloading explosives. Never drop, throw, or roll packages with explosives.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation (DOT) Emergency Response Guidebook lists all hazardous chemicals and their identification numbers.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These are called placards.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous products are also flammable. Take proper safety steps if your cargo may be flammable.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, what must you have?
questions.explanation: You must have a written route plan when transporting explosives and follow it. Avoid crowded areas, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys whenever possible.

questions.question: Where should you NOT keep hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt.
On the driver's seat when the driver is outside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or somewhere the driver can easily see and reach while driving. If the driver leaves the vehicle, place papers on the driver's seat.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tires with your hand.

questions.explanation: You must check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only accurate way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The dangers or risks of the material.
Where to place items on the trailer.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The dangers or risks of the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. Each hazard class shows what dangers or risks come with that material.

questions.question: How do you show the difference between hazardous and non-hazardous materials on a shipping paper?

options.text: List hazardous materials at the bottom.
List hazardous materials at the top.
Highlight hazardous materials in the same color as non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: List hazardous materials at the top.
questions.explanation: You can show hazardous materials in three ways: list them first, highlight them in a different color, or mark them with an "X" in a column labeled "HM".

questions.question: What letters must appear on shipping papers and packages for reportable quantity materials?
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous materials in a reportable quantity, the shipper must put the letters "RQ" on both the shipping paper and the package.

questions.question: What must a package with liquid containers display?

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must show arrows pointing the correct way up. Place these packages in the correct direction.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are products that pose risks during transportation. These include explosives, flammable gases, poisonous gases, and flammable or dangerous solids.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, where should placards be placed?

options.text: On all four sides of the vehicle.
Only for Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards must be placed on all four sides of any vehicle transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the correct placards?

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: To pick the right placards, you need to know the hazard class of the materials, how much is being shipped, and the total weight of all hazard classes in the vehicle.
